newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 7.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Monday:

* Philippine shares were seen moving in a narrow band of 20 points as the prevailing high interest rates were dampening investor interest, said Helen Alvarez, research director of All Asia Capital and Trust Corp.
* "There is no positive news to reverse sentiment," said DBS Securities analyst Al Rillo, adding that calls for a devaluation of the peso were hurting the equities market.
* On Friday, the Philippine stocks composite index closed 16.54 points higher at 2,758.96.

* The U.S. financial and equities markets were closed on Friday due to the Independence Day holiday. The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 100.43 points up at 7,895.81. PLDT's ADR closed up $1 1/4 at $65 3/8.
* The Philippine peso closed higher at 26.399 to the dollar against 26.405.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was up at 24.40625 percent vs 24.3125 percent.

* Shares of PLDT climbed to a two-year high on Friday and other firms with large export earnings followed suit as talk of the peso weakening over the next few days swirled in the market, analysts said.
* The total foreign currency deposits of commercial banks in the Philippines increased to $16.58 billion as of June 20 this year, the Central Bank said.
* Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc said it had decided to slow down the launching of new projects, keeping it only one for the rest of the year.
* Liquor firm La Tondena Distillers Inc had secured a one billion peso syndicated loan from a group of domestic financial institutions, syndicate manager All AsiaCapital and Trust Corp said.
* Keppel Philippines Holdings Inc said its first quarter net rose by 20 percent to 30 million pesos.

* BusinessWorld reported quoting sources that the Office of the President will review the government's foreign exchange policy following calls from exporters as well as economists to allow the peso to depreciate.
* The Philippine Central Bank was seen selling dollars at 26.40 pesos in early trade on Monday, traders said.
* Philippine annualised consumer inflation rate rose to 4.8 percent in June from 4.2 percent in May, the National Statistics Office said on Friday.
* A Reuters poll showed oil refiner Petron Corp was expected to post a 14.65 percent rise in net profit for the first six months of 1997 to 2.27 billion pesos from 1.98 billion pesos a year ago.
